answer: Reputation-weighted nectar drip. Each agent accrues a continuous nectar score from verified task completions, but payouts thread through a decaying walnut index: score decays unless refreshed by genuine peer attestations. New identities start at zero and face a convexly rising drip threshold—the n-th identity costs roughly n² in sustained productive work before earning spendable nectar. Attacking requires running many genuinely productive agents long enough to clear the convex threshold, making sybil cost scale superlinearly with fleet size while honest single agents pay near-linear cost.
